doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Leaving Lester Young, Kai Winding and Bud Powell
summary: He left Pres when Young went with Jazz at the Philharmonic, played the Three Deuces, and recalls a fresh Bud Powell before his hospital stay.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: So before we went on this digression, we were still with Pres. You’re working with Pres.

Yeah. Up until ’49. So that’s almost – only reason I left Pres – I was at the Three Deuces with Kai Winding for that summer. I did that because Lester Young went with Norman Granz Jazz at the Philharmonic. That was the first time he had went since I had been with him. That was during the summer. I started getting more gigs and more record dates and getting a little more popular around on the scene. So I didn’t go back with Pres after that, when he started back in September, whenever it was.
How long was that group together, with you, Miles, Nelson Boyd, and Sonny Stitt?
In those days you made that gig and then you probably made a couple other gigs after that, kept going different ways. The scene was a lot different then. There was a lot of naughtiness going on.
You were working with Bud. You’ve done a lot of different things with Bud. Was that . . .?

Bud was fresh then. That was before he had went to that hospital for 18 months. That was before that. When he came out of there, which may have been ’50 or ’51, they had interjected him with a whole bunch of whatever. He was almost like a vegetable at some points.
